Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • 3-day history of profuse loose/watery diarrhea (≥4 episodes today, “lost count”), vomiting of all oral intake including fluids, subjective fever (“literally boiling”), peri-umbilical abdominal pain that precedes urge to defecate.  
  • Recent close contact with brother who has identical symptoms; probable infectious gastroenteritis.  
  • Risk of dehydration.

- Relevant family medical history:
  • Brother currently unwell with similar gastroenteritis.  
  • No chronic familial diseases mentioned.  

- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • Vitamin D supplement daily (dose/route not documented).  
  • Ibuprofen PRN for dysmenorrhea (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
  • Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) sachet solution, ~3 × daily for past 2 days (dose not documented).

- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.  

- Sexual and reproductive health:
  • Last menstrual period: 2 weeks ago; usual dysmenorrhea.  
  • Not on contraception; not in regular sexual relationship.  
  • No pregnancies or STIs mentioned.

- Physical activity and nutrition:
  • States she “eats well” normally; no detailed dietary intake.  
  • Physical activity level not discussed.

- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  • Non-smoker.  
  • Drinks “a pint from time to time” (exact frequency/units not recorded).  
  • Denies illicit drug use.

- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.

- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Not recorded.

- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.

- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:

  • Works as a graphic designer; currently working from home due to illness.  
  • No caring responsibilities noted.

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not ordered.

  • Hydration assessment planned (likely basic bloods, not yet done).

Management Plan

- Arrange urgent in-clinic appointment today for:  
  • Stool specimen collection for culture to rule out bacterial gastroenteritis.  
  • Clinical assessment of hydration status; consider blood tests and IV fluids if indicated.  
- Continue Oral Rehydration Salts: small, frequent sips; monitor urine output.  
- Dietary advice: bland foods (toast, biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, milk until recovery.  
- Safety-net: Attend ED if symptoms worsen, inability to keep fluids down, reduced urine output, or new red-flag features (blood in stool, severe pain, persistent high fever).  
- Telephone support line number provided for escalation.  
- No medications prescribed at this stage; review after stool results.  
- Work certificate/discussion as needed once assessed in clinic.

Consider (for future / preventive care):
- Offer comprehensive preventive health review (e.g., immunisations, cervical screening, mental health check) at follow-up.  
- Discuss CTG registration and allied health plans when acute issue resolved.

• Missing but clinically expected elements: objective vitals (BP, pulse, temp), weight/BMI, urinalysis, immunisation status review, alcohol intake quantification, detailed mental health screening, smoking history confirmation, cervical screening status, STI screening, vision/hearing checks.  
• Internal contradictions: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; occasional pauses and minor inaudible words but clinical details obtainable.
